rv.q: Scott Thomas quick-changes her way between premiers and decades with massive reserves of enjoyment and empathy. This dame makes a hell of a Queen.
Beyond Caring has a slow pace, its characters are taciturn - but they do actually clean.
Entertaining all this, but unadventurous. It panders to easy anti-intellectualism, suggesting that the Queen's 'ordinariness' (what?) is a bulwark against damaged, overachieving PMs.
The problem really is Morgan's blandly amusing but desperately trivial script.
